sourceFile: "REVISED_by_LRS_Cycle_of_Prayer_24-25_v.2.pdf" (25 pages, titled internally "CYCLE OF PRAYER 2025 - 2026"), fetched via curl from https://files-backend.assets.thrillshare.com/documents/asset/uploaded_file/3308/Edsd/504fa799-f956-49bf-b648-9e5a6a60f12a/REVISED_by_LRS_Cycle_of_Prayer_24-25_v.2.pdf?disposition=inline and cross-checked against rendered page images.
notes: URL note: the source URL's own filename ("REVISED_by_LRS_Cycle_of_Prayer_24-25_v.2.pdf") reads "24-25", but the PDF's own title page and every internal heading read "CYCLE OF PRAYER 2025 - 2026" / "2025- 2026" -- confirming the prayer-roster's own research note that the filename is stale. This file transcribes the document's actual printed content (2025-2026), not the filename.

Granularity: unlike the roster's own pre-fetch research note (which described the source as week-range-keyed, one subject per week), the actual 25-page PDF is a genuine DAILY cycle. Each printed weekly heading (e.g. "November 30 - December 06, 2025") is only a page-layout grouping; within it, every individual calendar day is separately numbered and carries its own distinct content -- usually a Sunday's parish list, but every other day of the week also has its own subject(s): a clergy birthday/ordination-anniversary line, a saint's day, a BCP prayer topic, a diocesan committee/deanery, etc. This file therefore records cycleType 'dated' with one entry per actual calendar date (`date` is that date itself, taken directly from the day's own printed day-of-month digit plus the week heading's month/year), not one entry per week.

Year-boundary handling: the source is one continuous daily cycle running from Advent 2025 (Sunday, November 30, 2025) through Christ the King Sunday 2026 (November 22, 2026), continuing in smaller print through November 27, 2026 before a blank 'For your personal Prayers and Concerns' page. This is the identical 'Advent [year-1] through Christ the King [year]' shape as this corpus's existing episcopal-atlanta-2026.json, episcopal-north-carolina-2026.json, and episcopal-oklahoma-2026.json, which all defer/exclude a similarly lopsided late-prior-year Advent lead-in rather than splitting into two files. Following that precedent: this file's `entries` begin at January 1, 2026 and the 2025 portion (Sunday, November 30, 2025 through Wednesday, December 31, 2025 -- 32 days, all falling within Advent/Christmas) is deferred/excluded entirely, not fabricated or merged into 2026. A future episcopal-south-dakota-2025.json could hold that excluded portion if wanted.

`liturgicalNote` records the day's own printed calendar/commemoration headline exactly as printed (Sunday titles, saints' days, 'Ash Wednesday', 'Ember Day', etc.) -- and, since the source does not typographically distinguish them from liturgical commemorations, this also includes the handful of civil/secular observances the source prints in that same headline slot on their own date: 'Labor Day', 'Memorial Day', 'Native American Day', 'United Nations Day', 'Thanksgiving Day'. When a headline is immediately joined on the same source line to an instructional clause (e.g. 'Labor Day, We give thanks to all types of workers...'; 'Ember Day-Pray for those in the ordination process.'; 'THE SIXTH SUNDAY OF EASTER (MOTHER'S DAY) & (Rogation Sunday) Pray for Mothers BCP p. 815 & for the Human Family'), the calendar name itself is recorded as `liturgicalNote` and the instructional clause is split out as its own `category` subject, rather than folding a full sentence into `liturgicalNote`.

On 16 dates the source's only printed content for that day is a bare calendar/commemoration headline with no separate prayer-focus line beneath it (e.g. 'THE PRESENTATION of our Lord Jesus Christ in the Temple', 'Ash Wednesday', 'St. Joseph', 'ASCENSION DAY', 'Thanksgiving Day'). Since this schema requires a non-empty `subjects` array, that same headline text is recorded both as `liturgicalNote` and, once, as a `category` subject on those dates, rather than inventing unrelated content or leaving `subjects` empty. Affected dates: Feb 2, Feb 18, Feb 24, Mar 19, Mar 25, Apr 25, May 14, Jul 22, Jul 25, Aug 6, Aug 15, Aug 24, Sep 14, Sep 21, Sep 28, Nov 26, 2026.

Two calendar days have no printed content in the source at all (confirmed by viewing the rendered PDF pages as images, not an extraction loss): March 9, 2026 (the source jumps from March 8 directly to March 10) and July 31, 2026 (the source jumps from July 30 directly to August 1). No entry is fabricated for either date.

Three day-numbering overflow/mislabeling errors in the source's own printed day-of-month digits were resolved by folding the misdated content into the nearest date it actually belongs to, rather than fabricating an impossible or duplicate date: (1) the 'December 28, 2025 - January 03, 2026' week block's final line, printed under day number '04' ('Pray for the Nation, BCP p. 838'), falls outside that block's own stated range and duplicates the following week's own Sunday date -- folded into the January 4, 2026 entry, appended after that Sunday's own parish content. (2) Likewise, the 'June 21-27, 2026' week block's final line, printed under day number '28' ('The Rev. Jean Mornard (o), Grace, Huron'), duplicates the next week's own Sunday (June 28) -- folded into the June 28, 2026 entry. (3) The 'July 12-18, 2026' week block prints day numbers 12 (Sunday), then 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 -- i.e. after the Sunday (already day 12), the source re-prints '11' and '12' before correctly resuming at '13'. Both mislabeled items ('Pray for the Eastern Deanery' and 'Pray for the Northwest Deanery' + its TEC camp note) are folded into the July 12, 2026 Sunday entry; the remaining items (Rosebud Deanery, Central Deanery, Northeast Deanery, Standing Committee, Thunderhead Committee, St. Mary's Board) are recorded on July 13-18 respectively, matching their own correctly-printed day numbers.

Sunday-ordinal-count errors preserved as printed, not corrected: August 30, 2026 is headlined 'THE 12TH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST' even though the preceding Sunday (August 23) was already 'THE 13TH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST' (an apparent regression in the source's own count); and October 4, 2026 is headlined 'THE 19TH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST' immediately after September 27's 'THE 16TH SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST' (skipping the 17th and 18th Sundays after Pentecost entirely in the source's own numbering). Both transcribed exactly as printed.

Two stray trailing digits, disclosed here rather than folded into transcribed `place` text: 'St. John's, Browns Valley, MN 31' (March 30) prints a trailing '31' with nothing following it (no separate March 31 entry exists -- see the missing-day note above); and 'Holy Spirit, Firesteel & Mediator, Kyle 04' (April 4, Holy Saturday) prints a trailing '04' self-referencing that same date. Both are dropped from this file's `place` values as apparent page-layout artifacts, not parish-name content. A few other lines carry a similar self-referential day-number in parentheses appended after other content; those are preserved verbatim rather than dropped, since they read as part of the sentence rather than a stray line-break artifact: 'Deacon Robyn Shores-Foster (o), Calvary Cathedral (05)' (January 5) and 'The Rev. Claude Vershure (o), Retired (23)' (July 23).

Companion Diocese of East Tennessee: nearly every Sunday's parish list pairs one or more Diocese of South Dakota congregations with a congregation of the companion Diocese of East Tennessee (marked 'TN' in the source). Every individually named congregation, from either diocese, is recorded here as a `parish` subject (name + place, including the Tennessee congregation's state abbreviation exactly as printed) rather than as `category`, since each is a specific, individually named congregation per this schema's own subjectShape definition of 'parish' -- not a diocese- or Communion-wide subject.

A few parish lists name a second congregation with no place of its own immediately after a first congregation that does name a place (e.g. 'St Peter's, Ft. Pierre, St. Mary's,  & Trinity, Gatlinburg, TN', September 20, 2026, where 'St. Mary's' has no town printed for it at all). In each such case this file infers the same town as the immediately preceding named congregation (here, St. Mary's is recorded at 'Ft. Pierre') rather than leaving the schema's required `place` field blank. This is a disclosed judgment call, not independently confirmed against the diocese's own parish roster.

The source's own legend reads 'Legend: (b)...birthday (o)...ordination' -- these abbreviations mark a clergy or lay leader's birthday or ordination anniversary, and a further name after '&' is typically that person's spouse. Both are preserved exactly as printed (not expanded or split out) within each affected `category` subject's `name`.

Excluded front/back matter: the PDF's first two pages (a standing prayer request for the Truth, Justice & Healing Commission on Native Boarding Schools, naming its members, followed by 'A Prayer to Remember the Innocents') are not date-keyed and are excluded from `entries`, consistent with this corpus's existing treatment of undated standing front matter (cf. episcopal-southwestern-virginia-2026.json's excluded standing companion-diocese sentence). The final 'For your personal Prayers and Concerns :' page (blank space for the reader's own notes) is likewise excluded as it carries no dated content.

Preserved typos/oddities transcribed verbatim rather than corrected: 'St. John the Baptist, Bullshead' (September 22) for 'Bullhead' elsewhere in the source; 'Thankful Memorial, Chatanooga, TN' (October 4) for 'Chattanooga'; 'Deacon Tom Regan, (b),' with a stray comma before '(b)' (January 19); a doubled '(b)' in 'The Rev. Dr. Ramona Hayes (b), St. Paul's, Brookings (b) and Tim' (February 9); a missing space in 'the 142ndDiocesan Convention' (October 3); and the same place named inconsistently across two separate occurrences -- 'Blessed Redeemer, Howe Creek' with no state (March 8) versus 'Blessed Redeemer, Howe Creek, NE' (November 23). Minor incidental comma/space formatting within a `place` value (e.g. 'Ooltewah,TN' vs. 'Ooltewah, TN' on different occurrences) has been normalized to a consistent 'City, ST' spacing without altering any wording.

The February 1, 2026 Sunday headline, 'The Fourth Sunday after the Epiphany', is printed in mixed case rather than the ALL-CAPS style used for every other Sunday headline in this source; preserved exactly as printed rather than normalized to match the others.

'The Diocese of South Dakota' is the source's own title-page name for itself ('The Diocese of South Dakota Cycle of Prayer'); the body of the document elsewhere refers to it without the leading 'The' ('Diocese of South Dakota').
